result.verdict: Not ship-ready for fast one-handed triage. The boards are visually coherent and error/undo states are unusually complete, but the core jobs are buried or ambiguous: Send, Reply, Archive and Cleanup are unlabeled icons in a moving side strip, Inbox grouping differs between outer and inner displays, and several confirmations/counts contradict each other. A first-time founder will not reliably know where they are, what the primary action is, or what just happened.

findings.element: Bottom-left circular '↑' Send button (New message / Reply)
findings.problem: Primary Send is an unlabeled up-arrow at bottom-left, while Edit draft replaces it with 'Done'. Users may tap Done expecting send, or miss Send entirely; 'Done', 'Retry' and a spinner also occupy the same spot in other states, so the slot does not mean one thing.
findings.norm: iOS Mail/Gmail convention: a clearly labeled, consistently placed Send affordance; a control position must keep a stable meaning. Minimum 44pt labeled target for a primary action.
findings.fix: Use a labeled 'Send' pill (arrow + Send) in one fixed place in every compose state. Use 'Save'/'Done' as a separate secondary control and never let Retry/spinner replace Send without a text label and status.

findings.element: '×' close button and paperclip/document icon in left side strip
findings.problem: Close and Attach are vertical icon-only buttons far from the From/To fields they affect. Attach icon changes from paperclip (New message) to a document icon (Edit draft / Cc suggestions) for the same job.
findings.norm: Related controls should be proximate and icons must be consistent for the same action across sibling states.
findings.fix: Keep one attach icon, place it adjacent to the body/attachment list, and label Close/Save behavior; keep the strip vocabulary identical across New, Reply and Edit draft.

findings.element: 'Discard prompt' sheet (Discard changes / Keep editing) vs 'Close with typed text' sheet (Save draft / Discard draft / Cancel)
findings.problem: Two close-with-content flows look and behave differently: one offers no save option and no Cancel, the other offers Save draft plus Cancel. Users cannot predict whether closing preserves work.
findings.norm: One destructive-exit pattern per app: Save draft / Discard / Cancel, with identical wording and placement.
findings.fix: Use a single action sheet for all compose exits with Save draft, Discard (red), Cancel; trigger it consistently from × and swipe-down.

findings.element: 'Sending' state bottom-left spinner; 'Not sent' state 'Retry' button
findings.problem: Sending shows only a small spinner replacing Send: no 'Sending…' text, no cancel, no indication the form is locked. On failure the same slot becomes 'Retry', so the user must re-learn the primary action at the moment of error.
findings.norm: Async primary actions show labeled progress, disabled fields, and a persistent recovery action next to the error, not in place of the main CTA.
findings.fix: Show an inline status bar 'Sending…' / 'Not sent — saved in Drafts' with Retry and Edit actions, keep Send visible but disabled during sending.

findings.element: 'Send result unknown' banner (We couldn't confirm this sent… Open Sent / Send again) and 'Mail changes off' banner
findings.problem: Multi-line warning text is tiny and wraps awkwardly; 'Send again' — which risks duplicate mail — is low-contrast text beside 'Open Sent'. The highest-risk action is the least prominent.
findings.norm: Error recovery must be plain-language, legible at arm's length, and the safe path (check Sent first) must be the visually primary path; risky duplicates need confirmation.
findings.fix: Full-width banner with heading 'Did it send?', primary button 'Check Sent', and 'Send again' behind a confirmation explaining duplicate risk.

findings.element: Attachment chip 'kickoff-agenda.md 4 KB ×' in New message
findings.problem: The small × on the chip is the only remove affordance and sits at the far right edge; there is no attachment count, add-another entry point near the chip, or preview on tap implied.
findings.norm: Attachments should support tap-to-preview and a ≥44pt remove target, grouped with the compose body.
findings.fix: Make the whole chip tappable for preview, enlarge the remove hit area, and keep an 'Add attachment' row directly below the body.

findings.element: Bulk action menu: 'Unsubscribe from 2 senders' + 'Skip inbox for future mail' above CTA 'Archive 101 emails' with 3 senders selected
findings.problem: Counts contradict: 3 senders are ticked but unsubscribe says 2, with no explanation of which sender is excluded or why. Choosing an item in this menu leaves the main CTA still reading 'Archive 101 emails', so the chosen intent appears lost.
findings.norm: Bulk-action summaries must reconcile counts (selected, archivable, unsubscribable) and the confirmation/CTA must restate the exact chosen action.
findings.fix: State '3 senders · 101 emails · 2 can unsubscribe' with per-sender badges, and make the CTA change to the selected action, e.g. 'Unsubscribe 2 + Archive 101'.

findings.element: 'Confirm' sheet: 'Archive 101 emails from 3 senders? You can undo this afterwards.'
findings.problem: Confirmation covers only archiving even after the user explored unsubscribe/skip-inbox, and 'You can undo' conflicts with the Done screen's 'Unsubscribing can't be undone.' Users may confirm believing all of it is reversible.
findings.norm: Confirmations must enumerate every effect, separating reversible from irreversible effects before commitment.
findings.fix: Confirm with a breakdown: 'Archive 101 emails (undoable). Unsubscribe from 2 senders (cannot be undone).' Require explicit acknowledgement of the irreversible part.

findings.element: Bottom split CTA 'Archive 101 emails' + separate '⌄' button
findings.problem: A chevron pill glued to the primary CTA reads as part of the button; users cannot tell it opens a different action menu (Unsubscribe/Skip). The persona's headline job — bulk unsubscribe — is hidden behind an unlabeled chevron.
findings.norm: Split buttons need a visually distinct menu segment; headline tasks must not be hidden behind icon-only overflow.
findings.fix: Label the segments: primary 'Archive 101' and a text 'More ▾' button, or offer three explicit action rows (Archive / Unsubscribe / Skip inbox) once ≥1 sender is selected.

findings.element: 'In progress' state: 'Archiving' button and enabled back '<' in side strip
findings.problem: No progress count (e.g. 40/101), no cancel, and back navigation appears available mid-operation with no statement of what leaving does. Long bulk jobs will be abandoned ambiguously.
findings.norm: Long operations show determinate progress, remain cancellable where possible, and define the effect of navigating away.
findings.fix: Show 'Archiving 40 of 101…' with a progress bar and Cancel; either disable back or state 'Archiving continues in background'.

findings.element: Clock icon in Cleanup side strip opening 'History'
findings.problem: History/undo-later is reachable only via an unlabeled clock glyph in the strip. After the Done toast disappears, founders have no discoverable path to undo a past cleanup except this icon.
findings.norm: Recovery/history for destructive bulk actions needs a labeled entry point (e.g. 'History' or 'Recently archived').
findings.fix: Add a labeled 'History' button in the Cleanup header and link it from the Done screen ('View in History').

findings.element: Inbox '…' More menu containing only 'Cleanup'
findings.problem: The founder's bulk-clean job is a single item hidden behind an unlabeled '…' at the bottom of the left strip, behind a chat FAB. First-time users scanning for 'clean up newsletters' will never find it; it also duplicates no visible entry elsewhere.
findings.norm: Top persona tasks need a labeled, persistent entry point, not sole residence in an overflow menu.
findings.fix: Surface a labeled 'Cleanup' action in the Inbox header/toolbar (with count, e.g. 'Clean up · 5 senders') and keep the menu item as a secondary path.

findings.element: Side-strip archive and reply icons in Message view (archive-box, curved arrow)
findings.problem: Archive and Reply are stacked icon-only glyphs in the left strip; the archive glyph reads as trash/delete, and Reply — the persona's key action — has no label or prominent button in the message footer. Tapping wrongly archives the message being read.
findings.norm: Mail convention: labeled Reply at the message footer and a clearly distinct Archive vs Delete icon; destructive-adjacent actions need separation and labels.
findings.fix: Add a full-width labeled 'Reply' button at the bottom of the message, move Archive to the header with a text label on first use, and use distinct Archive (box) vs Delete (trash, red on confirm) icons.

findings.element: 'After Archive: next message opens' — 'Intro: design partner' with 'Archived / Undo' bar
findings.problem: Archiving silently teleports the user into a different sender's message with no position context ('next in Needs reply'), no way back to the archived message except a transient Undo. Fast triage users lose their place and may reply to the wrong thread.
findings.norm: Auto-advance after archive must be announced, reversible, and show queue position; users need an explicit setting/behavior cue.
findings.fix: Show 'Archived Ana Ruiz — showing next (2 of 3). Undo' and return to the list instead of auto-opening unless the user opted into auto-advance.

findings.element: Thread view collapsed rows (Ana Ruiz Oct 17 / You Oct 18 / Ana Ruiz)
findings.problem: Earlier messages collapse to one-line rows with no chevron, quoted-text cue, or '2 earlier messages' label; the only expansion affordance is guessing a tap. The current message is not visually marked as the expanded one beyond spacing.
findings.norm: Collapsed thread items need an explicit expand affordance and count; the open message must be clearly identified.
findings.fix: Add '▸ 2 earlier messages' affordance with chevrons/snippet expansion and highlight the expanded message header.

findings.element: Attachment preview header 'pilot-timeline.pdf 212 KB' and bottom-left share glyph
findings.problem: Preview shows skeleton grey lines instead of document content at full height, with no page count, zoom, download or 'Open in…' — only an unlabeled upload/share icon in the strip. Users cannot verify the timeline they were sent.
findings.norm: Document preview must render content (or state why it cannot), with page indicator, zoom and a labeled Share/Open action.
findings.fix: Render the PDF pages with page indicator and pinch-zoom; if rendering fails show 'Can't preview — Download / Open in Files' with labeled buttons.

findings.element: Bottom chat-bubble FAB and 'Inbox agent didn't respond / Try again' toast
findings.problem: The AI agent — central to the product brief — is an unlabeled speech-bubble FAB present on every screen; nothing says 'Ask Inbox agent'. Its failure toast mimics the archive-failure toast, so agent errors and mail errors are indistinguishable.
findings.norm: AI entry points need a label/name and error copy that names the failing system and offers a next step.
findings.fix: Label the FAB 'Ask' with the agent name on first run, and use distinct copy: 'Inbox agent timed out — your mail is unaffected. Retry / Dismiss'.

findings.element: Left side control strip (back, search, filter, compose, '…', agent) on outer Inbox
findings.problem: Six small unlabeled targets are split between the top and bottom of a narrow left strip next to the Dynamic Island: Compose (pencil) sits far from the Inbox title, '…' and agent are detached at the bottom, and nothing has a text label. One-handed reach and learnability are poor, and the strip's contents change between states (e.g. No mail account keeps only '<').
findings.norm: iOS convention places search, compose and overflow in predictable header/tab-bar positions with labels or standard placement; navigation chrome must be stable across states of the same screen.
findings.fix: Move to a conventional layout: title + search at top, labeled Compose FAB bottom-right within thumb reach, Cleanup in '…', and keep the same chrome in empty/error states.

findings.element: 'To do' card (Confirm Thursday kickoff / Add bank details) above 'Needs reply 3' list
findings.problem: The card duplicates messages that also appear as rows below (Ana Ruiz kickoff, Acme Payroll bank details), so the same work is counted twice and tapping either copy has an unexplained relationship. It also appears on the outer Inbox but is absent from the inner Split Inbox, so triage order differs by display.
findings.norm: A task must have one canonical representation; grouped prioritization must be consistent across form factors of the same app.
findings.fix: Either make To do the only representation (rows move into it) or mark card items as shortcuts that highlight the row; replicate the same grouping model on inner displays.

findings.element: Swipe-left reveal: 'Spam' and 'Archive' blocks on Example Weekly row
findings.problem: Spam and Archive appear as near-identical dark-grey blocks with tiny icons, no color separation (destructive vs neutral), and the swiped row's text is clipped mid-sentence ('g — Notes, shaders, and more'). A fast swipe risks marking legitimate mail as Spam.
findings.norm: Swipe actions follow iOS conventions: distinct colors, Archive neutral and Spam/Delete treated as consequential, full-swipe action explicitly chosen and undoable.
findings.fix: Color-code (Archive grey/blue, Spam orange/red), add text labels at partial swipe, require confirmation or Undo for Spam, and keep row content from clipping (fade, don't truncate mid-word).

findings.element: 'First sync' skeleton rows under 'Syncing your mail'
findings.problem: Skeleton bars give no progress, elapsed expectation, mail count, or completion criteria, while search/filter/compose remain tappable against an empty data set. Users cannot tell a stuck sync from a slow one.
findings.norm: First-run sync must communicate progress, expected duration, and disable or explain actions that need data.
findings.fix: Add progress ('Fetching mail… 1,240 messages'), a background-completion note, and disable compose/search until first data lands or explain their state.

findings.element: 'Consent needed' screen 'Let the Inbox agent read your mail?' with Allow / Not now
findings.problem: The consent copy ('It sorts mail and drafts replies. You approve anything it sends.') does not state scope (which account, history depth), retention, or how to revoke — yet gates the entire Inbox behind an otherwise empty screen with only a back arrow. 'Not now' destination is undefined.
findings.norm: Mail-reading consent must name data scope, purpose, retention and revocation path, and the decline path must lead to a usable state.
findings.fix: Expand consent with account, scope, 'change anytime in Settings', and make 'Not now' land on the plain (agent-off) Inbox with the agent FAB disabled and explained.

findings.element: Inner sidebar: 'Personal ▾', '+ New', PAGES (Inbox/Finance/Legal/Cap table/Data room/Artifacts), PERSONNEL agents
findings.problem: '+ New' does not say new what (page, message, agent?). Page status text ('6 mo runway', '2 deadlines', '3 need reply') is tiny low-contrast grey; agent rows (Chief, Finance agent, Carta agent, Legal agent) use cryptic colored glyphs with no role description, so a founder cannot tell bots from pages from people.
findings.norm: Creation buttons name the object created; navigation must distinguish content types with labels, and status metadata needs ≥4.5:1 contrast.
findings.fix: Make '+ New' a menu (New message / Page / Agent), add section captions explaining Pages vs Agents, and raise status text size/contrast with labeled badges.

findings.element: Inner Inbox vs outer Inbox control placement and density
findings.problem: On the inner display the control strip mirrors to the right edge, search becomes a header field ('Search mail'), Cleanup disappears entirely, and only ~6 messages fill an 890×626 canvas above a large empty area — while the outer display crams To do + Needs reply + Today in a denser, differently grouped list. Folding the device remaps muscle memory and loses the cleanup workflow.
findings.norm: Split-view adaptations keep the same actions in analogous positions and use added width for an additional column/value, not empty space.
findings.fix: Keep strip side/actions consistent across displays, retain a labeled Cleanup entry, and use inner width for list + preview (as in Inner-Message) or a triage summary column instead of void.

findings.element: Inner message view: list + 'Re: Pilot timeline' panes
findings.problem: There is no selected-message triage navigation (no next/previous, no 'Needs reply 1 of 3'), no Reply button in the reading pane — only small archive/reply glyphs in the right strip and a '…' — and the left pane header changed to '< Personal' (outer used back to Inbox), so returning to the full Inbox list is ambiguous. Attachment rows also lost the '>' affordance they have on the outer message view.
findings.norm: Two-pane mail must preserve selection context, offer sequential triage controls, a labeled Reply, and consistent row affordances across panes/form factors.
findings.fix: Add labeled Reply + Archive in the message header/footer, prev/next with '1 of 3 in Needs reply', a clear '‹ Inbox' back control, and restore attachment chevrons matching the outer view.

findings.element: Timestamp and secondary metadata type (10:30 AM, Oct 18, 'to me') across list and message screens
findings.problem: Timestamps, snippets and status pills (Draft ready, Needs attention, Newsletter, Junk) use small, low-contrast grey/yellow text on dark backgrounds, with inconsistent formats (Oct 19, 10:30 AM vs 10:30 AM vs Oct 17). Scanning priority by time — the triage task — is unnecessarily hard.
findings.norm: WCAG AA contrast for metadata, one relative/absolute date convention per surface, and priority signaled by weight/position, not only tiny pills.
findings.fix: Standardize on one date format, raise metadata contrast/size, and give Needs-reply rows a persistent visual treatment (weight + dot + pill) instead of pills alone.

excellent: PG-A-Cleanup.png — Done/Empty/History states are exemplary: '3 senders cleaned up · 101 emails archived · 2 unsubscribed', a persistent Undo, an honest 'Unsubscribing can't be undone', and a dated History prove bulk actions are recoverable.

PG-A-Compose.png — Validation and send-failure coverage is thorough and honest: invalid address shows inline 'Not a valid address', 'Not sent. Your message is saved in Drafts', and 'Sending is off… Turn on' names the account and the fix.

Sheet.png — Inbox zero, No mail account ('Connect Gmail'), Gmail needs reconnecting and Changes-to-mail-are-off states each give one clear next action instead of a dead end; 'Archived / Undo' and 'Couldn't archive / Try again' keep the row in place on failure.

PG-A-InboxMessage.png — Newsletter unsubscribe is modeled responsibly: a persistent 'Unsubscribe from Example Weekly' row plus a confirmation that correctly marks the action in red and says 'This can't be undone.'

PG-A-Cleanup.png — Selection math is communicated in the CTA itself ('Archive 101 emails', '3 senders selected', disabled 'Archive' when nothing is selected), so users see consequences before confirming.

result.verdict: Praci establishes a sleek, high-contrast dark UI with thoughtful edge-case coverage (uncertain send states, mail-changes-off safety switches, AI agent consent, and sender-grouped cleanup). However, several P0/P1 workflow and state-consistency flaws directly block the founder persona from reaching Inbox Zero fast: AI-prepared drafts ('Draft ready') vanish when opening the message, the 'Edit draft' screen replaces the Send button with 'Done' leaving no way to send the draft, bulk Cleanup fails to disclose irreversible unsubscribes in its confirmation prompt, and outer-display Undo toasts jump to the top-right corner out of thumb reach.

findings.element: Primary action button in 'Edit draft' frames ('Done' button at bottom-left control rail)
findings.problem: In 'Edit draft', 'Cc suggestions', 'Invalid address', and 'Discard prompt', the bottom-left primary action button changes from the Send icon ('↑') to 'Done', leaving no Send button anywhere on the screen. A founder editing a draft reply has no way to actually send the email.
findings.norm: Editing a draft email must always provide a direct 'Send' primary action; saving/closing drafts is handled automatically or via the close/back control.
findings.fix: Keep the primary bottom-left circle button as 'Send' ('↑') in 'Edit draft' frames, and handle 'Save draft / Discard changes' via the 'X' close button or auto-save.

findings.element: 'Draft ready' message thread ('Re: Pilot timeline' from Ana Ruiz)
findings.problem: In Sheet.png ('Inbox'), the top thread from Ana Ruiz ('Re: Pilot timeline') displays a prominent 'Draft ready' badge (created by the Inbox AI agent). However, when the user opens that exact message in PG-A-InboxMessage.png ('Message' and 'Thread') or Inner-Message.png, the prepared draft is completely missing—forcing the user to manually compose a reply from scratch.
findings.norm: When an inbox row advertises an AI-prepared 'Draft ready', opening the thread must immediately surface the draft inline (with 1-tap 'Send' or 'Edit') to fulfill the promise of fast triage.
findings.fix: Display an inline 'Draft ready' composer card at the bottom of the opened message thread with direct 'Send' and 'Edit' actions.

findings.element: Cleanup 'Bulk action menu', 'Confirm' sheet, and 'Done' state
findings.problem: In 'Bulk action menu' (Frame 4), tapping the split chevron next to 'Archive 101 emails' shows 'Unsubscribe from 2 senders' without indicating whether it replaces or combines with archiving, or which 2 of the 3 ticked senders support unsubscribe. Then, 'Confirm' (Frame 5) asks 'Archive 101 emails from 3 senders? You can undo this afterwards' with zero mention of unsubscribing—yet 'Done' (Frame 8) states '101 emails archived · 2 unsubscribed' and warns 'Unsubscribing can't be undone.'
findings.norm: Irreversible bulk actions (unsubscribing) must be explicitly reflected in the primary CTA and disclosed in the confirmation dialog before execution, never revealed as irreversible only after completion.
findings.fix: Show per-sender 'Unsubscribe available' metadata in the list, make 'Also unsubscribe (2)' an explicit toggle or combined CTA ('Archive & Unsubscribe'), and state in the Confirm modal that unsubscribing from 2 senders cannot be undone.

findings.element: Top toast banner in 'Archived, Undo' and 'Archive failed, row stays'
findings.problem: In Sheet.png (Frames 3 and 4), the 'Archived [Undo]' and 'Couldn't archive [Try again]' toasts appear at the very top of the screen, occluding the 'Inbox' title and placing the time-critical 'Undo' button in the top-right corner—the hardest area to reach one-handed. Conversely, in PG-A-InboxMessage.png (Frames 7–9), the exact same toast components sit at the bottom of the screen in the thumb zone.
findings.norm: Transient action feedback and 'Undo' toasts must maintain a consistent spatial location across the app and reside within easy one-handed thumb reach at the bottom of the viewport.
findings.fix: Move the 'Archived [Undo]' and 'Couldn't archive [Try again]' banners in Sheet.png to the bottom of the content column, matching PG-A-InboxMessage.png.

findings.element: Inner display master-detail view ('Inner-Message.png') vs 'Split.png'
findings.problem: In Split.png, the Inbox has 'Search mail', 'Filter', and 'Compose' controls. As soon as the user opens a message in Inner-Message.png, the left pane still shows the Inbox list, but 'Search mail', 'Filter', and 'Compose' completely disappear from the UI, and the only navigation is '< Personal' (which exits Inbox back to the workspace sidebar).
findings.norm: In a dual-pane master-detail inbox layout, global list tools (Search, Filter, Compose) should remain accessible while a message is open in the detail pane.
findings.fix: Keep Search, Filter, and Compose accessible in the Inbox list header or control rail while viewing a message on the inner display.

findings.element: Inbox row triage badges across 'Sheet.png', 'Split.png', and 'Inner-Message.png'
findings.problem: Triage badges behave inconsistently across screens showing the exact same inbox state: in Sheet.png, Ana Ruiz has 'Draft ready' and 3 other emails have 'Needs attention', 'Newsletter', and 'Junk'. In Split.png, Ana Ruiz's 'Draft ready' badge disappears while the other 3 remain. In Inner-Message.png, all 4 badges ('Draft ready', 'Needs attention', 'Newsletter', 'Junk') vanish completely from the Inbox list.
findings.norm: Critical semantic triage badges ('Draft ready', 'Needs attention', 'Newsletter', 'Junk') must persist consistently across outer, split, and master-detail views.
findings.fix: Retain 'Draft ready' on Ana Ruiz in Split.png and preserve all row status badges in the left inbox list of Inner-Message.png.

findings.element: 'To do' summary card at top of Inbox ('Sheet.png' Frame 1 vs Frames 2–4 and 'Split.png')
findings.problem: In Sheet.png Frame 1 ('Inbox'), a 'To do' card ('Confirm Thursday kickoff', 'Add bank details for payroll') sits at the top of the Inbox. In Frames 2, 3, and 4 (when swiping or archiving a newsletter further down the list), as well as in PG-A-Cleanup.png Frame 1 and Split.png, the 'To do' card vanishes completely without explanation.
findings.norm: Pinned header modules ('To do') should not disappear during row swipe gestures or toast animations, and should be consistently represented on the inner display.
findings.fix: Keep the 'To do' card consistent across Inbox interaction states in Sheet.png (or provide an explicit collapse toggle) and include it in Split.png.

findings.element: Left rail control strip in 'PG-A-InboxMessage.png' vs 'Inner-Message.png'
findings.problem: On the inner display (Inner-Message.png), opening an email shows a 'More' ('⋮') button in the control rail. On the outer display (PG-A-InboxMessage.png), there is no 'More' ('⋯') button at all—only Back, Archive, Reply, and AI Chat—leaving outer-display users with no way to mark unread, report spam, delete, or move an open message.
findings.norm: Secondary message actions (Delete, Spam, Mark unread, Move) must be reachable from the open message view on both outer and inner displays.
findings.fix: Add the 'More' ('⋯') button to the left control rail in PG-A-InboxMessage.png.

findings.element: Reply button in 'PG-A-InboxMessage.png' ('Message' and 'Reply menu')
findings.problem: Tapping the Reply icon in PG-A-InboxMessage.png opens a 3-option popover ('Reply', 'Reply all', 'Forward') even though the email from Ana Ruiz is addressed only 'to me' (single recipient), adding an extra tap to every reply. Furthermore, PG-A-Compose.png ('Reply, title menu open') already allows switching between Reply, Reply all, and Forward inside the composer.
findings.norm: For single-recipient emails—and for fast mobile triage—tapping Reply should immediately open the Reply composer in one tap, with long-press or the composer header menu used to switch to Reply All or Forward.
findings.fix: Make single-tap on the Reply icon open the Reply composer immediately (or default to Reply/Reply All appropriately), reserving the menu for long-press or the '⋯' overflow menu.

findings.element: Cleanup sender list in 'Nothing selected' and 'Senders ticked'
findings.problem: Cleanup opens with 0 senders selected, offers no 'Select all' action, and provides no way to preview or expand which 48 emails are inside 'Example Weekly' before bulk-archiving them.
findings.norm: Bulk cleanup tools should support 'Select all / Deselect all' for speed and allow users to drill into a sender row to verify its emails before archiving.
findings.fix: Add a 'Select all' action in the Cleanup header, separate the checkbox tap target from the row body, and add a right chevron ('>') on each sender row to preview its messages.

findings.element: Send button ('↑') in 'Send result unknown' and 'Mail changes off' ('PG-A-Compose.png' Frames 13 & 14)
findings.problem: In Frame 13 ('Send result unknown'), the inline warning banner offers a 'Send again' action while the bottom-left Send ('↑') button also remains active, creating duplicate competing triggers. In Frame 14 ('Mail changes off'), the banner states 'Sending is off for me@example.test', yet the bottom-left Send ('↑') button remains bright white (enabled) instead of disabled.
findings.norm: When sending is blocked by account settings, the primary Send button must be visually disabled; when a retry action exists, there should be a single unambiguous trigger.
findings.fix: Disable/dim the bottom-left Send ('↑') button in 'Mail changes off' (Frame 14), and unify the retry trigger in 'Send result unknown' (Frame 13) so the banner and bottom-left rail do not conflict.

findings.element: Attachment button icon in 'PG-A-Compose.png' (Frames 4–8 vs Frames 1–3, 9–14)
findings.problem: The third circular button in the left control rail shows a paperclip icon in 'New message' and 'Reply' (Frames 1–3, 9–14), but inexplicably switches to a blank document/page icon in 'Edit draft', 'Cc suggestions', 'Invalid address', 'Discard prompt', and 'Close with typed text' (Frames 4–8).
findings.norm: An action button in a fixed control rail must use a consistent icon across all states of the same composer screen.
findings.fix: Use the paperclip attachment icon consistently across all 14 frames of PG-A-Compose.png.

findings.element: 'Cc, Bcc' row and quoted thread expander ('...') across 'PG-A-Compose.png'
findings.problem: In Frame 1 ('New message'), the 'Cc, Bcc' row is visible, but in Frames 8–14 (which are also 'New message' states), the 'Cc, Bcc' row disappears completely. Similarly, Frame 2 ('Reply') includes a '...' button to expand the quoted thread, whereas Frame 4 ('Edit draft' for the same 'Re: Pilot timeline' reply) omits the '...' quoted-message expander.
findings.norm: Header fields ('Cc, Bcc') and thread context expanders ('...') should remain consistently available across all states of composing or editing a draft.
findings.fix: Keep the 'Cc, Bcc' collapsible row or inline affordance in all 'New message' states, and include the '...' quoted-thread toggle in 'Edit draft' states.

findings.element: Expanded message in 'Thread' (Frame 4) vs 'Message' (Frame 1) in 'PG-A-InboxMessage.png'
findings.problem: In Frame 1 ('Message'), Ana Ruiz's Oct 19, 10:30 AM email contains two paragraphs, a sign-off, and two attachment pills ('pilot-timeline.pdf', 'kickoff-agenda.md'). In Frame 4 ('Thread'), that exact same Oct 19, 10:30 AM message is missing its second paragraph, sign-off, and both attachment pills.
findings.norm: The latest expanded message in a thread view must display its full body and attachments identically to the single-message view.
findings.fix: Include the full message body and both attachment cards on the expanded Oct 19 message in Frame 4 ('Thread').

findings.element: Left swipe actions ('Spam' and 'Archive') in 'Swipe left: Archive, Spam' ('Sheet.png' Frame 2)
findings.problem: Swiping left on 'Example Weekly' reveals 'Spam' right next to 'Archive' with equal visual weight, while clipping the row text mid-character ('g — Notes, shaders, and more') and hiding the sender name. Placing a destructive 'Spam' action immediately adjacent to 'Archive' on a left-swipe risks accidental spam reports during rapid one-handed triage.
findings.norm: Standard mail clients separate 'Archive' (primary left swipe) from destructive/secondary actions ('Spam', 'Unsubscribe', 'Snooze') via opposing swipe directions or distinct color coding, and truncate text cleanly with ellipses.
findings.fix: Truncate the swiped row cleanly while keeping the sender name visible, and either move 'Spam/Unsubscribe' to right-swipe or style 'Archive' as the distinct primary swipe action.

findings.element: Unread indicator dots and section titles across 'Sheet.png', 'Split.png', and 'Inner-Message.png'
findings.problem: In Sheet.png, the 3 emails under 'Needs reply 3' have no unread dots while 'Acme Payroll' and 'Example Weekly' under 'Today' have white unread dots. In Split.png and Inner-Message.png, the unread dots are inverted: the 3 'Needs reply' emails and 'Acme Payroll' have unread dots, while 'Example Weekly' does not. Additionally, the section title 'Today' in Sheet.png becomes 'Other mail today 24' in Split.png, and the sidebar count reads '3 need reply' while the list header reads 'Needs reply 3'.
findings.norm: Unread state indicators, section naming, and badge phrasing must be synchronized across outer and inner displays.
findings.fix: Standardize the unread dot states, align the section header ('Today' vs 'Other mail today'), and unify phrasing ('3 need reply' vs 'Needs reply 3') across all screens.

findings.element: Keyboard overlay in 'New message, keyboard open' ('PG-A-Compose.png' Frame 9) and PDF card in 'Attachment preview' ('PG-A-InboxMessage.png' Frame 3)
findings.problem: In PG-A-Compose.png Frame 9, the system keyboard spans full width across the dedicated left control strip column whereas bottom modal sheets (Frames 7 & 8) stay confined to the right content column. In PG-A-InboxMessage.png Frame 3 ('Attachment preview'), the white PDF card bleeds flush into the right screen edge with 0pt right padding while maintaining padding on the left and bottom.
findings.norm: Screen-level layout margins and rail boundaries should be respected consistently by child surfaces and previews.
findings.fix: Add matching right margin (12–16pt) to the PDF preview card in 'Attachment preview' and ensure consistent column behavior between the left control strip and bottom overlays.

findings.element: More menu button ('⋯' vs '⋮') and single-item 'Cleanup' menu ('PG-A-Cleanup.png' Frame 1, 'Split.png')
findings.problem: In PG-A-Cleanup.png Frame 1, tapping the '⋯' button opens a popover containing only a single item ('Cleanup'), making the overflow menu redundant. Furthermore, the More button uses a horizontal ellipsis ('⋯') on the outer display (Sheet.png) but switches to a vertical ellipsis ('⋮') inside the exact same circular button on the inner display (Split.png, Inner-Message.png).
findings.norm: An overflow menu ('⋯') should not be used to wrap a single action, and icon orientation for the same button should stay consistent across displays.
findings.fix: Either surface 'Cleanup' directly as its own icon button in the rail/header (or include other inbox actions in the '⋯' menu), and use '⋯' consistently on both displays.

excellent: Comprehensive operational edge-case design: 'Send result unknown' (preventing duplicate emails by prompting to check Sent), 'Mail changes off' (safe read-only mode), 'Consent needed' (clear AI agent permission boundary), and 'Cleanup History' with post-action Undo are remarkably thoughtful.

High-signal workspace sidebar in Split.png: surfacing live operational metrics directly next to page names ('Inbox: 3 need reply', 'Finance: 6 mo runway', 'Legal: 2 deadlines') and AI agents as approachable team members under 'Personnel' fits the startup founder persona.

Clean dark-mode typography and visual restraint: generous contrast, crisp hierarchy between sender/subject/snippet, and scannable status pills ('Draft ready', 'Needs attention', 'Newsletter') make the inbox immediately legible at a glance.
